transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-30 16:00 PDT | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Avery Chen, Marco Ruiz (Redwood) — Priya Nair, Elliot Brooks, Samir Patel, Jocelyn Park (Sunset Gridworks)

Auto-generated sections (may contain errors):
Summary: Quick kickoff to align runbook and roles; security questions; confirm SLA targets.
Topics captured: runbook, VPC, KMS, SOC two, pilot metrics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery, I'm the CSM on the account, and with me is Marco from the SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Morning — thanks, Avery. We're good. Excited to get this started. Quick intro from our side: I'm Priya, head of platform — Elliot is SRE, Samir is our security lead, Jocelyn is product.
[00:22] Marco Ruiz: Great to meet you all. I wanted to say up front we'll try to keep this practical — runbook, who-owns-what, and then the SLA/latency tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated.
[00:33] Elliot Brooks: Yep, and we want to make sure the network bits are clear — VPC peering or a private connect is our preference for the pilot.
[00:42] Samir Patel: And from security, we'll need KMS integration + proof of SOC2 controls. Also curious about audit logs retention.

[01:05] Avery Chen: Perfect — agenda for today: runbook walkthrough, roles, SLA primer, then open Q&A and next steps. Marco, do you want to take the runbook section?
[01:12] Marco Ruiz: Sure. So the runbook we use for onboarding has these sections — onboarding checklist, network/connectivity, auth and IAM, deployment mapping, monitoring and alerting, and rollback/playbook. Note: the autogenerated notes sometimes call our console 'Redwood Console' or just 'console' — the transcript might show variations.
[01:35] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Can you clarify what 'deployment mapping' includes?
[01:40] Marco Ruiz: Yeah — basically model version mapping to environments (staging, pilot, prod), and how traffic routing/policies work: canary, traffic split, automatic fallback to smaller models. We'll include a diagram in the runbook.

[02:10] Jocelyn Park: For the pilot we want to validate quality first then ramp cost optimizations, so mapping versions is important — we may want to pin a model family for the first 2 weeks.
[02:22] Marco Ruiz: Totally. We recommend pinning to a model variant for the pilot so you avoid regressions. Then Redwood Optimize will give quantization and batching suggestions once we have traffic profile.

[03:05] Elliot Brooks: On the network side — do you support VPC peering and private IP endpoints? We can't route over the public internet for the pilot.
[03:13] Avery Chen: Yes, for Private deployments we provide a private control plane option and VPC peering. For Hosted, we have options with private endpoints and dedicated capacity with reserved pools. Note: sometimes folks confuse 'private control plane' with on-prem package — we'll send clearer docs.
[03:35] Samir Patel: Ok, KMS — do you allow customer-managed keys? We need to know where keys live and whether Redwood can rotate them.
[03:43] Marco Ruiz: Customer-managed keys (via KMS/HSM) are supported on Private and Dedicated deployments. For hosted we can integrate with customer KMS in a VPC setup; rotation policies are supported but have operational considerations. We'll include exact flow in the security pack.

[04:20] Priya Nair: Audit logs — how granular are they? We need token-level traces and per-request metadata persisted for 90 days.
[04:28] Avery Chen: We do token-level cost and latency breakdowns and per-request traces. Retention is configurable — for enterprise we can extend retention. We'll include the retention settings in the runbook and the pricing implications.

[05:05] Jocelyn Park: About SLAs — our product requires a p95 latency under 400ms for real-time features. Can Redwood hit that consistently?
[05:13] Marco Ruiz: Depends on model choice and batch settings. For smaller models and optimized kernels on dedicated GPUs, p95 sub-400ms is achievable. For larger context windows or larger models, you'd want either dedicated capacity or a hybrid routing policy. There's a tradeoff between latency and unit cost. We'll run a profiling session against a sample workload to give a firm answer.

[06:00] Elliot Brooks: Is there an easy way to fail over to a cheaper model when latency spikes? We want graceful degradation.
[06:07] Marco Ruiz: Yes — routing policies can automatically fall back to compatible variants and regions. We'll show the policy config in the runbook. Sometimes the transcript substitutes 'regions' for 'regimes' — ignore that.

[07:00] Samir Patel: A couple security questions: SAML SSO for admin access, RBAC, and whether admin audit logs are tamper-evident.
[07:09] Avery Chen: SSO/SAML and SCIM are supported; RBAC is granular. Audit logs are stored in append-only storage and we can provide a signed export for compliance requests. We'll attach SOC 2 artifacts.

[08:01] Priya Nair: For the pilot timeline — we're aiming for a two-week pilot starting mid-June. Is that feasible?
[08:08] Avery Chen: Yes — two weeks is common. Week one: integration + smoke tests, week two: load + quality checks. We'll align specific dates in the shared doc.

[08:45] Marco Ruiz: For integration checklist: API keys, network allow-list, model pinning, sample prompts, and a small benchmark harness. We'll provide a starter harness you can run locally or in your environment.

[09:30] Jocelyn Park: About billing — do you give estimates before we run the pilot? We need to budget for the dedicated pool if needed.
[09:38] Avery Chen: Yes, once Marco runs profiling and we collectively estimate token volumes and peak QPS, we'll provide cost estimates and show the difference between hosted vs dedicated.

[10:10] Elliot Brooks: On compliance: can we run a short SOC2 questionnaire and get answers in a week?
[10:15] Samir Patel: (overlaps) we need the compliance pack quick.
[10:18] Marco Ruiz: We can send the security questionnaire today and aim to return answers within 3-5 business days. Some attachments like SOC two report PDFs will be provided.

[11:00] Priya Nair: Network diagram — can you share an example showing how the VPC peering looks with private control plane? We need to show it to our networking team.
[11:07] Avery Chen: Absolutely. We'll attach a network diagram in the runbook package; it shows VPC peering, private endpoints, and optional on-prem connectors.

[12:00] Jocelyn Park: Are there any gotchas with prefix/KV cache? We do lots of short conversational interactions.
[12:07] Marco Ruiz: Prefix caching and KV cache can save tokens on repeated context. For chat-heavy workloads we recommend a cache policy and a sticky session config. We'll recommend TTLs in the runbook based on your sample prompts.

[13:20] Elliot Brooks: For the SE deep-dive — what telemetry should we collect? CPU/GPU metrics, token breakdown, end-to-end p95?
[13:28] Marco Ruiz: Exactly. Collect per-request token counts, model latency breakdown (decode vs attention), and GPU throughput. We'll give a template.

[14:10] Samir Patel: One more security nuance: do you provide a private deployment option that can be air-gapped? We may have a future need.
[14:18] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we offer an on-prem package for highly regulated or air-gapped workflows. It's heavier lift but supported — we'll include the uplift/conops in the docs.

[15:30] Avery Chen: Ok let's do a quick recap of owners and dates. Action items I'll list in the follow-up email. Marco will run the profiling and set up the SE deep-dive. Priya will share traffic patterns. Samir will send the security questionnaire items.

[16:05] Priya Nair: One slight ask — can you include sample dials for batching and quantization suggestions? Our cost team wants a matrix.
[16:12] Marco Ruiz: Yes, Redwood Optimize will provide a matrix for batching/quantization vs expected cost savings and quality delta. We'll include a first-pass matrix in the runbook.

[17:00] Jocelyn Park: Timeline check — we should lock pilot start by June 13th to align with a product milestone in late June.
[17:08] Avery Chen: We'll target June 13th start. Action items to confirm by next Friday.

[18:00] Elliot Brooks: Any blockers for IAM integration? Our IAM team uses Okta and expects SAML plus SCIM provisioning.
[18:08] Marco Ruiz: Okta SAML + SCIM is supported. We'll include setup steps and sample metadata exchange in the docs.

[19:00] Samir Patel: Small note — please call out differences in encryption at rest between hosted and private.
[19:07] Marco Ruiz: Good point — hosted encryption is provider-managed by default; private/dedicated supports customer-managed KMS keys. We'll be explicit.

[20:00] Avery Chen: Alright, I want to flag the next sync — SE deep-dive the week of June 7th and a go/no-go check-in the week of June 7th or 10th. Does that work?
[20:12] Priya Nair: Works for us.
[20:18] Jocelyn Park: We'll prepare sample prompts and a small dataset for profiling.

[21:00] Marco Ruiz: I'll drop a calendar invite for the deep-dive and include a pre-read with what to run.

[22:00] Priya Nair: Anything else on your side?
[22:05] Samir Patel: No, I'll wait to see the security pack.
[22:10] Avery Chen: Great — thanks everyone. We'll send the runbook and attachments within 24 hours. Recap in the follow-up with owners.

[22:30] Jocelyn Park: Thanks all.
[22:32] Elliot Brooks: Thanks.
[22:34] Marco Ruiz: Thanks, bye.

Notes about transcript: automated transcription had some minor substitutions (e.g., 'SOC two' instead of 'SOC 2', 'KV cache' occasionally split as 'K V cache'). There was brief crosstalk at 10:15–10:18.

End of transcript.
